renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: pr_curve
  title: Precision and recall across thresholds
  description: |-
    Each point is the precision and recall of the SNP calls that pass one variant quality threshold, joined into a curve. It answers how much recall is given up to buy precision when the callset is filtered harder.
    How to read: a curve that stays near the top right across thresholds means the quality score separates true from false calls well. A curve that drops fast as recall falls means filtering removes true calls as readily as false ones. Pick the threshold where precision stops improving.
    Lines and annotations: the area under the curve is computed from the swept points of this table, so it is a data-defined summary and not a published cut-off. Recall is TP over TP plus FN and precision is TP over TP plus FP, as hap.py defines them.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Illumina/hap.py/master/doc/happy.md
  kind: roc_pr_curve
  roles:
    recall: recall
    precision: precision
    threshold: quality

- component: table
  title: Threshold sweep
  description: |-
    Each row is a quality threshold with the recall, precision and F1 of the SNP calls kept at it. It answers the exact numbers behind the curve.
    How to read: find the row with the highest F1 to pick a threshold that balances the two, or read down the recall column to see where it starts to fall.

- component: figure
  title: F1 by variant type
  description: |-
    Each bar is the F1 score of the callset against the truth set for one variant type, with all calls and passing calls side by side. It answers how accurate the calls are for SNPs and for indels, and what the filter changes.
    How to read: a bar near one means the callset agrees with the truth. A pass bar clearly above its all bar shows the filter removed false calls, and equal bars show it removed none.
    Note: F1 is the harmonic mean of recall and precision, and the cited hap.py documentation states no cut-off for it, so none is drawn.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Illumina/hap.py/master/doc/happy.md
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: variant_type
    y: f1
    color: filter
    barmode: group
    labels:
      variant_type: Variant type
      f1: F1 score
      filter: Filter

- component: table
  title: Benchmark summary
  description: |-
    Each row is a variant type and filter with the true positives, false negatives and false positives and the recall, precision and F1 recomputed from them. It answers the counts behind the F1 bars.
    How to read: a low recall with a high precision means the callset misses truth variants, and the reverse means it calls false ones.
